newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors buying CompuServe calls.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors buying CompuServe calls.

text.p: Investors continued to snap up calls of CompuServe Corp after it said it was in talks with a third party regarding a possible business combination, traders said Wednesday.
But investors in America Online Inc were trying to digest the situation, leaving options volumes in that stock relatively light.
Rumors that AOL was in talks to buy CompuServe surfaced Tuesday and continued Wednesday after the Washington Post, citing industry sources, said AOL was exploring a purchase of CompuServe.

On Wednesday, CompuServe and H&R Block Inc, which owns about 80 percent of the online service company, said discussions were under way with a third party about CompuServe, but there was no assurance that the talks would result in any agreement or transaction.
AOL had declined to comment on the buyout speculation and later declined to comment on the CompuServe-H&R Block announcement.
"CompuServe has been really busy the last few days -- a lot of call buying," a market maker in the options said. "It started two days ago."

CompuServe options trade on the American Stock Exchange (AMEX), Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) and the Philadelphia Stock Exchange, but the market maker said most of the action was on the AMEX and CBOE.
"Today all we have is call buyers," he said, adding that front-month volatilities were up about 20 points to around 90 percent.
The April 10 call traded a total of 660 contracts, the April 12-1/2 call traded 860 and the April 15 call traded about 180. The May 10 call traded more than 600.
CompuServe shares, which were halted intraday, finished 1-5/8 higher at 12-5/8. Turnover topped three million shares.
Traders said activity in AOL options was muted.
"There's not a lot of option activity," a market maker in AOL options said. "I think a lot of people don't know how to interpret the situation.
"There's a lot of uncertainty out there," he said, adding that volatilities on AOL options have been on the rise.
"But it's more in anticipation of something happening, not from a lot of options buyers," he said. "There have been some (buyers), but not a lot."
AOL shares ended down 1-1/8 at 44-5/8 after trading up to 46-3/4 and down to 43-1/4.
Among AOL options, which trade on the CBOE, AMEX and Pacific Exchange, the April 40 call traded a total of 414 contracts and the April 45 call traded more than 1,400.
On the put side, the April 40 traded 1,270, the April 45 traded 291 and the April 47-1/2 traded about 365.
